## RAW FINDINGS: Consus/Multica Coupling Sweep — `rip-out-consus-coupling`

### FILES_EXAMINED

**Dedicated Consus modules (candidates for full deletion):**
- `src/consus-decisions.ts` (97 lines) — `postQuestionToConsusDecisionApi()`, builds+POSTs a decision-request payload to `MINERVA_CONSUS_DECISIONS_URL` (default `http://localhost:8722/api/decisions`), 750ms timeout, fails soft. Exported `buildConsusDecisionRequest` too.
- `src/consus-poller.ts` (141 lines) — `pollConsusAnswers()` (registered ABI method), `findParkedConsusQuestions()`, `fetchConsusQuestionStatus()`. Reads `CONSUS_URL` (default `http://localhost:8722`), `MINERVA_CONSUS_POLL_TIMEOUT_MS`. Imports `extractAnswerFromItem` from consus-resume.ts (cross-module dependency between the two "dedicated" files).
- `src/consus-resume.ts` (367 lines) — `resumeFromConsusAnswer()`/`resumeAnsweredConsusDecision()` (both registered ABI methods), plus `fileStoriesToMultica`/`fileAllStoriesToMultica` (Multica CLI shell-out, duplicated near-verbatim from plan-runner.ts), `extractAnswerFromItem`/`extractAnsweredConsusDecision` (Consus item-shape parsers consumed by consus-poller.ts). Its own header comment claims "core ABI remains provider-neutral... this module is the thin Multica/Consus-aware hook path" — true for this file in isolation, but see kickoff-engine.ts below.
- `src/consus-auto-resume.ts` (87 lines) — `pollAndResumeConsusAnswers()` (registered ABI method), pure wiring: poll then resume, sequential.

**Core files with Consus/Multica-aware logic mixed into otherwise-generic code (surgical removal, not full deletion):**
- `src/dispatch.ts` — imports and registers all 4 Consus ABI methods in the `handlers` map alongside the 7 provider-neutral ones (`capabilities, startRun, getRunStatus, listRuns, getQuestions, submitAnswers, getOutput, abortRun`). `capabilities()` itself (`src/capabilities.ts`) returns only `{abi_version: "1.0.0"}` — it does **not** enumerate method names, so removing the 4 methods does not change the `capabilities` wire response. The method list is documented only in `docs/architecture.md`'s markdown table, not runtime-introspectable.
- `src/kickoff-engine.ts` — `recordTurn()` (called from both `startRun` and `submitAnswers`, i.e. every turn) calls `await postQuestionToConsusDecisionApi(runId, question)` **unconditionally**, no flag gate. On a truthy `posted.posted` it flips `status` to `"awaiting-consus"` and stamps `consus_question_id` onto the question. This is inside the CORE turn-recording path, not an add-on module — genuinely load-bearing per the "known" map.
- `src/run-manager.ts` — `RunStatus` union includes `"awaiting-consus"` (line 14); `Question` interface (not `RunRecord`) carries `consus_question_id?: string` (line 64 — note: the "known" map says "RunRecord has a first-class consus_question_id field," but it is actually on `Question`, nested inside `RunRecord.questions[]`, not a top-level `RunRecord` field — worth correcting). Also: `defaultSeedRepoPath()` returns `~/repos/consus-seeds` and its error message references `git clone git@github.com:mdostal/consus-seeds.git` — **this is a separate, distinct "Consus" hit**: a seed-repo naming convention, not the Consus service. The triage queue (`.pHive/triage/queue.yaml` t-002) explicitly scopes this OUT as "a small, unrelated test-hygiene bug already tracked as its own story" — do not conflate with the service rip-out.
- `src/plan-runner.ts` — confirmed ~24 references. `CONSUS_URL` env default `http://localhost:8722`; `pollConsusForAnswers` flag on `PlanRequest` (properly opt-in, only engaged when `req.pollConsusForAnswers` truthy in `runHeadlessPlan`'s while-loop); a **separate, unconditional-when-pending** "surface parked questions to Consus" block at the end of `runHeadlessPlan` (lines ~137-170) that POSTs every pending question to `${CONSUS_URL}/api/questions` regardless of the `pollConsusForAnswers` flag — this block is best-effort/non-blocking but is NOT gated the same way the poll loop is, contradicting the "known" map's characterization of plan-runner.ts as cleanly-gated. Also contains the full Multica CLI shell-out surface: `_multicaRunner`/`multicaJson`/`__setMulticaRunnerForTest`, `resolveIdeaFromTicket`, `fileStoriesToMultica`/`fileAllStoriesToMultica` (duplicate implementation of the same-named functions in consus-resume.ts).
- `bin/minerva.ts` — the CORE CLI entrypoint (the one `docs/architecture.md` AD-1 describes as "the entire external surface"). It imports all 4 Consus modules directly and offers `--poll-consus`, `--poll-and-resume`, `--consus-item-file`, `--file-to-multica` as alternate CLI modes baked into `mainArgs()`. This is not a separate integration binary — it's the same executable that also serves plain ABI dispatch via stdin. Its own `ARG_HELP` string is literally titled `"minerva — JSON-over-stdio by default, plus Consus resume shorthand"`.

**Isolated/legitimate integration entrypoints (structurally separate, worth distinguishing from core coupling):**
- `bin/minerva-plan.ts` (221 lines) — router-facing (`Auriga`-invoked) headless "plan a ticket" CLI. Imports `runHeadlessPlan, resolveIdeaFromTicket, fileAllStoriesToMultica` from `plan-runner.ts`. Always calls `runHeadlessPlan({..., pollConsusForAnswers: true, ...})` — i.e. this binary's own invocation of plan-runner.ts hardcodes the Consus-poll flag to `true` (not itself exposed as a CLI flag/opt-out here). `--file-to-multica` is a genuine opt-in CLI flag. Not imported by dispatch.ts or any core module — self-contained entrypoint, matches its header comment's "thin Multica-aware integration entrypoint" framing reasonably well, MODULO the hardcoded `pollConsusForAnswers: true`.
- `bin/ideate-to-consus.mjs` (627 lines) — a large, deliberately-named, self-contained Node ESM CLI (zero imports from `src/`). Its own header: "the MISSING HALF of the Pantheon ideation loop... FILE them into CONSUS as a decision item." Structurally distinct from every other Consus touchpoint: it never calls Consus's HTTP API directly — it POSTs/reads through a **Janus seam** (`${JANUS_URL}/api/seam/consus/${capability}` and `/api/seam/read/consus/decisions`, default `JANUS_URL=http://localhost:8726`), i.e. it already goes through a broker/adapter layer rather than hardcoding Consus's own port/API. It also independently resolves and shells out to the `multica` CLI (its own `multicaBin()`/`getTicket()`, separate from plan-runner.ts's/consus-resume.ts's implementations — three independent Multica-shell-out implementations exist in this repo). It is invoked standalone (not part of `dispatch`, not part of the ABI, no test coverage found for it — no `ideate-to-consus.test.*` file exists). Writes output under `docs/ideation/<slug>/` (confirmed real output at `docs/ideation/pan-6965/`).

**ABI/architecture docs:**

But its own "Data Model" section's `Run.status` (line 234) and the API Contract table's `getRunStatus` row (line 197) list only `in_progress | waiting_on_human | complete | aborted` — **`awaiting-consus` is absent from both**, even though `src/run-manager.ts`'s actual `RunStatus` type includes it. Doc/code drift already exists independent of any rip-out.
- `README.md` — architecture mermaid diagram's "internals" subgraph lists dispatch's method set as `capabilities · startRun / getQuestions · submitAnswers · getOutput / getRunStatus · listRuns · abortRun` — the 4 Consus methods are **not shown at all**, i.e. README's own diagram is already out of sync with dispatch.ts's actual handler registry. Separately, README's top-level "Architecture" flowchart and "How it fits" section both name `"Delphi / Consus\n(human decision surface)"` as a single conceptual sibling-god node.
- `VISION.md` — "② Goals — near-term next steps" lists **"Wire the decision surface. Connect the human-channel questions to the live Delphi / Consus surface"** as *future, not-yet-done* work — directly contradicted by the fact that `kickoff-engine.ts` already unconditionally posts to Consus today. Doc says "not yet wired," code says "wired unconditionally, no gate." Also confirms the internals diagram omits `forked`/consus methods (lists `ForkedHiveDriver (stub — not implemented)`, consistent with a snapshot predating the Consus work).

Combined with the triage finding below, this strongly implies Consus is Delphi under a different/renamed identity, not a separate god.

Multica, or votem at all — those are v2 infrastructure upgrades." This is a pre-existing, documented product requirement that the current Consus/Multica coupling already violates — the rip-out restores compliance with Minerva's own founding spec, not new policy.

- `.pHive/triage/queue.yaml` (t-002) — **a near-complete pre-existing brief on this exact problem**, filed 2026-08-14, state `prioritized`, priority `p0`/severity `critical`. Contains: the same 6 findings as this task's "known" map (slightly more precise — correctly identifies `consus_question_id` as a `Question` field, not `RunRecord`), an explicit **"Consus (renamed from Delphi)"** statement (resolves the naming ambiguity above), live evidence of the 20-test-failure breakage, and a `DECISION` entry timestamped 2026-08-14T14:34Z recording the operator's exact "full rip it out and apart" directive with a stated acceptance bar: re-run the pause/resume PoC from epic `minerva-value-audit` against the ripped-out code plus the already-shipped `fix-startrun-heimdall-routing` fixes.

### PATTERNS_OBSERVED

1. **Two structurally distinct coupling shapes exist, not one.** (a) *Core-woven*: `dispatch.ts` (registry), `kickoff-engine.ts` (unconditional call inside the load-bearing `recordTurn`), `run-manager.ts` (type system) — Consus-only, no equivalent Multica presence in any of these three files. (b) *Adapter-confined*: `plan-runner.ts` + `bin/minerva-plan.ts` — both Consus and Multica appear here, but behind explicit params/flags (`pollConsusForAnswers`, `--file-to-multica`), and the module's own header comment explicitly claims "core ABI stays provider-agnostic... this module + bin/minerva-plan.ts are the thin integration entrypoint." That claim is **accurate for Multica** (Multica never appears in dispatch.ts, kickoff-engine.ts, or run-manager.ts at all) but **inaccurate as a description of the whole system's Consus coupling**, since kickoff-engine.ts's call is not thin/optional/adjacent — it's inside the core turn-recording path every `startRun`/`submitAnswers` call goes through.
2. **Three independent Multica-CLI-shell-out implementations exist**, near-duplicated: `src/plan-runner.ts` (`_multicaRunner`/`multicaJson`/`fileStoriesToMultica`), `src/consus-resume.ts` (same function names, separate implementation, separate `__setMulticaRunnerForTest` seam), `bin/ideate-to-consus.mjs` (`multicaBin()`/`getTicket()`, its own PATH/env resolution). No shared Multica client module.
3. **`bin/ideate-to-consus.mjs` never talks to Consus directly** — it exclusively goes through a Janus seam (`/api/seam/consus/*`). This is the one place in the repo where Consus access is already behind a broker abstraction rather than a raw `fetch(CONSUS_URL...)` call.
4. **Consistent port default**: every direct-fetch Consus reference (`consus-decisions.ts`, `consus-poller.ts`, `plan-runner.ts`) defaults to `http://localhost:8722`. `ideate-to-consus.mjs`'s Janus default is a different port (`8726`) and a different service.
5. **Fail-soft-but-unconditional is the dominant Consus call pattern**: every direct Consus call (decisions POST, poller GET) has a short timeout (750ms) and catches all errors — it never throws, it degrades to "Consus unreachable, proceed as if not posted." This means the coupling doesn't crash callers, but it silently and non-deterministically changes returned `status` values (`waiting_on_human` vs `awaiting-consus`) depending on ambient network reachability — exactly the test-flakiness mechanism triage t-002 already caught live.
6. **A working "fail-open external dependency" precedent already exists in this codebase**: `agnostic-plan-driver.ts`'s Heimdall-route lookup is explicitly documented as "BULLETPROOF CLAUDE FALLBACK... returns null on ANY doubt." `driver.ts`'s `SpawnDriver` Heimdall call (t-003) is the negative counter-example (non-fail-open, breaks startRun in a stock environment). Neither is Consus-related, but both are directly relevant prior art for how an optional external call *should* be structured in this codebase if anything Consus-shaped survives.

---

### CONSTRAINTS

- `docs/product-brief.md` and `docs/initial-info.md` both state, as an already-approved v1 requirement, that Minerva must have **zero dependency on Delphi, Auriga, Vulcan, Multica, or votem existing**. The rip-out is corrective, not novel policy — this materially affects how the design-discussion team should frame it (compliance restoration, not a breaking API redesign for its own sake).
- `docs/architecture.md`'s AD-5 ("the stall invariant has no timeout... resume-from-disk IS pause/resume") and "No Autonomous Progress" are core, load-bearing architectural guarantees that must survive the rip-out untouched — the generic `waiting_on_human` + `submitAnswers` pause/resume mechanism is Minerva's actual core value proposition (per the operator's own question, "what is left of minerva at the end"), and is entirely independent of Consus. `awaiting-consus` is a Consus-specific enum value layered on top of, not underneath, this generic mechanism — removing it should not require reinventing park-and-wait, only deleting the extra state.
- `consus-poller.ts` depends on `consus-resume.ts` for `extractAnswerFromItem` — the two "dedicated modules" are not independent; deletion order/atomicity matters if done incrementally.
- `bin/minerva.ts` is the single external CLI surface (AD-1: "the entire external surface"). Removing its Consus imports changes real, currently-documented CLI flags (`--poll-consus`, `--poll-and-resume`, `--consus-item-file`, `--file-to-multica`) that are described in its own `ARG_HELP` output — any external caller currently scripting against these flags breaks.
- `docs/architecture.md`'s API Contract table is the closest thing to a formal spec for `pollConsusAnswers`/`pollAndResumeConsusAnswers` as documented ABI methods (full param/return rows) — removing them is a documented-contract change, not merely a code change, even though `capabilities()` itself never exposed a method list at the wire level.

---

### RISKS

- **Silent behavior change for real callers.** `bin/minerva-plan.ts` (the actual Auriga/`minerva-dev`-agent-invoked entrypoint per `docs/minerva-dev-agent-instructions.md`) hardcodes `pollConsusForAnswers: true` on every `runHeadlessPlan` call. If Consus polling is removed from `plan-runner.ts` without updating this call site, `bin/minerva-plan.ts` either breaks at compile time (best case) or silently no-ops a parameter that used to matter (worse case, if the field is just ignored).
- **`types.test.ts`'s exhaustive switch on `RunStatus`** will fail to compile the moment `"awaiting-consus"` is removed from the type unless the test is updated in the same commit — a mechanical but easy-to-miss coupling point between `run-manager.ts` and its own test suite.
- **ABI/documentation contract break**: if `pollConsusAnswers`/`pollAndResumeConsusAnswers`/`resumeFromConsusAnswer`/`resumeAnsweredConsusDecision` are removed from `dispatch.ts` without updating `docs/architecture.md`'s API Contract table, the doc will claim methods exist that return `UNKNOWN_METHOD` — a documented-but-broken contract, worse than the current undocumented-but-working README/architecture.md drift already present.
- **`docs/minerva-dev-agent-instructions.md`** is a live, apparently-in-use operator instruction set for a "minerva-dev" agent persona that references `--file-to-multica` and Multica ticket workflows as its primary mode of operation ("YOUR TOOL LIVES IN mdostal/minerva... run Minerva's headless kickoff+plan... file the decomposed stories back to Multica"). If Multica coupling in `plan-runner.ts`/`bin/minerva-plan.ts` is removed or gated behind a new opt-in mechanism, this doc (and any live agent persona configured against it) needs simultaneous updating or it will describe a workflow that no longer functions as written.
- **Duplicate Multica-shell-out logic** (`plan-runner.ts` vs `consus-resume.ts`) means a rip-out that only touches one of the two `fileStoriesToMultica`/`fileAllStoriesToMultica` implementations leaves the other behind, silently forking behavior between the two entrypoints that use them (`bin/minerva-plan.ts` vs `bin/minerva.ts`).
- **`ideate-to-consus.mjs` has no test file** — any rip-out work here (should it be touched at all) has zero regression-test coverage backing it, unlike every other Consus/Multica touchpoint in `src/`.

---

### UTILITIES_AVAILABLE

- `src/test-cli.ts`: `mockConsusServer()` and `mockHeimdallServer()` — reusable local-HTTP-server test doubles; `mockHeimdallServer` is Consus-independent and would remain useful regardless of rip-out scope.
- `__setMulticaRunnerForTest` seam exists independently in both `plan-runner.ts` and `consus-resume.ts` — an established dependency-injection pattern in this codebase for shelling out to external CLIs in tests, already proven, reusable for whatever adapter design replaces direct coupling.
- `agnostic-plan-driver.ts`'s `resolveAgnosticPlanDriver()` "returns null on ANY doubt" pattern — a working, tested, in-repo template for "fail-open, core never depends on this being reachable."

### EXTERNAL_REFERENCES

- Live Consus service on this dev machine, port 8722 (`lsof -i :8722`, `curl localhost:8722/api/decisions` — both confirmed responsive per triage t-002, consistent with what this session's setup also observed).
- Janus service, default port 8726, referenced only by `bin/ideate-to-consus.mjs`.
- `multica` CLI — resolved three different ways across the repo (`plan-runner.ts`/`consus-resume.ts`: bare `execFileSync("multica", ...)` relying on PATH; `ideate-to-consus.mjs`: explicit path search across `MULTICA_BIN`, `~/.local/bin/multica`, `/opt/homebrew/bin/multica`, `/usr/local/bin/multica`).
- `~/repos/consus-seeds` (git remote `git@github.com:mdostal/consus-seeds.git`) — the default seed repo for greenfield `fresh_init`/worktree allocation in `run-manager.ts`. Confirmed by triage t-002 to be an unrelated naming coincidence, explicitly out of scope for this rip-out (tracked separately as test-hygiene work in the `minerva-value-audit` epic).
- `plugin-hive`'s sibling repo `hive/references/task-tracking-adapter-abi.md` — the ABI spec Minerva's own wire format is stated to reuse; not itself Consus/Multica-coupled but is the format all of dispatch.ts's methods (including the 4 Consus ones) currently speak.

### UNANSWERED_QUESTIONS

- Is "Consus" formally confirmed (outside this session's inference) to be the renamed/successor identity of "Delphi" referenced throughout `docs/product-brief.md`, `docs/initial-info.md`, `.pHive/CONTEXT.md`, and `README.md`'s "Delphi / Consus" diagram label? The triage entry (t-002, line 81) states this as fact ("Consus (renamed from Delphi)") but this researcher found no equivalent confirmation inside this repo's own commit history or code comments — it may be operator/tribal knowledge not fully documented in-repo. This materially affects whether "the decision surface" concept itself is legitimate future v2 scope (just needs to go behind a contract) or should be excised entirely.
- Whether `bin/ideate-to-consus.mjs`'s Janus-seam pattern is the intended model Pantheon wants ALL Consus-touching code to use (i.e., "go through Janus, never hit Consus directly") — if so, that's a materially different rip-out shape (route everything through the seam) than "delete all Consus code from Minerva."
- Whether `bin/minerva-plan.ts` and `bin/ideate-to-consus.mjs`, as standalone entrypoints not wired into `dispatch.ts`'s ABI, are considered "Minerva" for purposes of the operator's "standalone god" bar, or whether they're allowed to remain Consus/Multica-integrated as separate, optional tools shipped in the same repo (the operator's own phrasing — "if it requires all of the others to do anything, then it is a process piece or a flag" — suggests the bar is about the core ABI/engine, but this wasn't explicitly resolved for the two standalone binaries).
- No test file exists for `bin/ideate-to-consus.mjs` — unclear whether that's an accepted gap (it's a standalone tool) or an existing test-coverage debt independent of this rip-out.

### INCONSISTENCY_RISK_SIGNALS

- `docs/architecture.md`'s own Data Model / API Contract tables **omit `awaiting-consus`** from `RunStatus`, while `src/run-manager.ts`'s actual type includes it — pre-existing doc/code drift, not caused by the rip-out but relevant baseline noise the design team should not mistake for a rip-out side effect.
- `README.md`'s dispatch method-list diagram **already omits** all 4 Consus ABI methods, while `docs/architecture.md`'s API Contract table **includes** them with full signatures — the two canonical docs already disagree with each other on what's part of the ABI, independent of any rip-out.
- `VISION.md` describes "wire the decision surface" as **not-yet-done, near-term future work**, while the actual code (`kickoff-engine.ts`) has had an unconditional Consus POST in the core turn path since the `minerva-auto-resume`/PAN-7523 commits. The vision doc and the shipped code have been out of sync for some time.
- The "known" research map's claim that `RunRecord` has "a first-class `consus_question_id` field" is imprecise — the field is on the nested `Question` interface (`run-manager.ts` line 64), not a top-level field on `RunRecord` (line 67-123 has no such field). Small but real correction for whoever plans the type-level rip-out.
- The "known" map's "5-commit minerva-auto-resume epic" undercounts actual history: `git log` shows the `minerva-auto-resume` epic itself (4 commits: store-parked-mapping, poll-consus-answers, resume-run-execution, e2e-verification) plus an *earlier*, separate PAN-7523/PAN-7524 pair ("post headless gates to Consus" / "resume Minerva plans from Consus answers"), plus separate "park to Consus inbox" commits (#31, #34) inside `plan-runner.ts`, plus the entirely separate `ideate-to-consus` feature's own ~6-commit history. Real Consus-touching commit count across the repo's history is at least 15+, spanning at least 3 distinct feature efforts, not one contained 5-commit epic.
- `.pHive/triage/queue.yaml` t-002 is dated 2026-08-14 with a `DECISION` entry timestamped `2026-08-14T14:34Z` recording this exact operator directive — this research task may be effectively duplicating/formalizing a triage item that already has a `prioritized` state and a stated PoC acceptance bar (re-running the `minerva-value-audit` pause/resume test).
